planting.note: Plant rooted divisions or container stock in spring in gritty, well-drained, neutral to alkaline soil in full sun; Nanum stays lower and tighter than the straight species without needing to be sheared into shape.

directions: Nanum is a naturally dwarf selection of wall germander that stays only a few inches tall while slowly spreading into a dense, glossy, oak-leaf-textured mat, making it useful as a very low edging or a boxwood-style miniature hedge without the clipping the straight species needs. Small pinkish-purple flower whorls appear along the mat through late spring and summer and bring in bees steadily. Give it sharply drained, lean, neutral to alkaline soil in full sun, since wet or heavy ground quickly causes root and crown rot. Mow or shear lightly once a year after bloom if an even, tighter mat is wanted, though the cultivar holds its low habit well without regular trimming.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Cherry Chief was selected by North Carolina plantsman Richard Dufresne for its uniquely translucent cherry-red flower color.

directions: Cherry Chief is an upright, spreading autumn sage selection bearing lightly fragrant racemes of translucent cherry-red flowers set off by dark red buds and deep purple calyces, a color that photographs poorly but glows in the garden from early summer into mid fall. Like other Salvia greggii selections it is an easy-care, drought-tolerant Texas native subshrub once established, and it draws hummingbirds throughout its long bloom season. Prune only after flowering finishes for the year, since cutting back earlier removes developing flower buds, and give it excellent drainage to avoid root rot in humid or wet-winter climates. A light shearing in late winter keeps older plants dense and floriferous.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock around last frost into fertile, alkaline to neutral, well-drained soil in full sun; Perfecta Alba is part of an RHS Award of Garden Merit series bred for extra-large, heavily frilled flowers.

directions: Perfecta Alba is a white-flowered member of the Perfecta series of Scabiosa caucasica, producing exceptionally large, ruffled pincushion flowers in pure creamy white on tall, wiry stems from midsummer into fall. The heavily frilled outer florets give each flower a fuller, lacier look than older caucasica selections such as Miss Willmott, and the long stems cut beautifully for arrangements. Plant in fertile, alkaline to neutral soil with sharp drainage, since this cultivar declines quickly in heavy or acidic ground, and deadhead regularly to keep new buds coming through the season. Divide congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigor, and provide good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew in humid climates.
